families.axis: flat report that something is not needed → reproach that nothing warranted it at all

members.gloss: not necessary
members.tone: The family's plain verdict - it states the thing was not needed and leaves any reproach implied rather than spoken, where *gratuitous* speaks it.

members.gloss: not necessary
members.tone: Flatter than *unnecessary* - it reports an absence of need without the faint blame that clings to the other word.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: Measures the overshoot rather than judging it: a quantity past the mark, not a fault.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: The easiest word here to hear without complaint - what lies beyond the requirement can simply be available, where *superfluous* would call the same amount waste.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: Sharper than *excess* - the surplus is treated as serving no purpose, not merely as a quantity over the line.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: Frames what is past the requirement as held in reserve, so it reads as usable rather than as clutter.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: Formal and weighty, marking the amount as going beyond what was required at all, with a dryness *extra* does not have.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: Dismissive where *excess* stays quantitative: it says the thing could be stripped away and nothing would be lost.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: Positional and countable - it sets something outside the number required without passing any verdict on it.

members.gloss: more than is needed, desired, or required
members.tone: A ledger word: it registers the amount left over as a balance and carries no complaint about it.

members.gloss: unnecessary and unwarranted
members.tone: The harshest of these - not merely that the thing was not needed, but that nothing justified it at all.

members.gloss: unnecessary and unwarranted
members.tone: Sounds the note of waste - unwarranted, and the sting is that it happened anyway; softer in rebuke than *gratuitous*.

members.gloss: unnecessary and unwarranted
members.tone: A rebuke rather than an assessment: it says the thing overstepped, where *unnecessary* only says it was not required.

members.gloss: not absolutely necessary
members.tone: The gentlest here - it grants that the thing may well be wanted and withholds only the claim that it is strictly required.

members.gloss: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
members.tone: Neutral and broad - it covers the animal, the plant and the uncultivated ground alike, naming the natural state without passing any verdict on it.

members.gloss: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
members.tone: The same natural state as *wild*, but framed as a taming that never happened, so it points at what has not been done to the thing.

members.gloss: wild and menacing
members.tone: Wildness with a threat inside it - the menace is carried by the word itself rather than read in, which is what *untamed* lacks.

members.gloss: wild and menacing
members.tone: The formal counterpart to *feral*, holding the same menace in a stiffer register.

members.gloss: wild and menacing
members.tone: The heaviest here - the menace lands as ferocity, where *feral* only marks the wildness as dangerous.

members.gloss: partially wild
members.tone: Purely a measure of degree - it places something part-way along the scale and judges it not at all.

members.gloss: not subdued or trained for service or use
members.tone: Defined against service - neither subdued nor trained to any use, so the wildness is measured by what the thing has not been made to do.

members.gloss: not domesticated
members.tone: A flat negation and nothing more, the plainest term in the family, with none of the menace *feral* adds.

families.axis: absurdity that draws open contempt → light, laughable foolishness

members.gloss: devoid of good sense or judgment
members.tone: The plain, unadorned charge that good sense or judgement is simply absent, with none of the mockery *ridiculous* invites.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Puts the unreasonableness first and lets the derision follow as a verdict, where *laughable* starts from the laugh.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Informal and offhand, treating the thing as skewed out of true and waving it away rather than arguing with it.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Carries the scorn in its own body: the thing is not merely open to derision but fit for nothing else.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Hits hardest of these, aiming the derision squarely at whoever produced the thing rather than at the thing itself.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Puts the derision in the response rather than in the thing - what is named is the laugh it draws, so it dismisses by amusement where *preposterous* repudiates out loud.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Theatrical, full-blown absurdity, grander than *laughable* and past the point where argument is possible.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Locates the failure in the sense itself, so nothing coherent is left to answer, where *absurd* still concedes a shape to reject.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Formal and indignant, repudiating the absurdity out loud rather than merely laughing at it as *laughable* does.

members.gloss: so unreasonable as to invite derision
members.tone: Blunt and immediate, the derision arriving without the argument *absurd* implies.

members.gloss: devoid of intelligence or thought
members.tone: Nothing at all stands behind it, neither intelligence nor thought, a flatter and heavier charge than *foolish*'s bad judgement.

members.gloss: devoid of intelligence or thought
members.tone: Formal and colder than *mindless*, treating the absence of intelligence or thought as a settled quality of the thing.

members.gloss: devoid of intelligence or thought
members.tone: Names the emptiness as blankness rather than stupidity, the intelligence and thought simply not in evidence.

members.gloss: ludicrous, foolish
members.tone: Almost fond, taking the foolishness as entertainment rather than a fault, a long way from *idiotic*.

members.gloss: ludicrous, foolish
members.tone: The gentlest word here, foolish and ludicrous at a scale too small to be worth condemning.

members.gloss: ludicrous, foolish
members.tone: Foolishness with energy behind it, off-kilter and lively where *silly* is merely slight.

families.axis: harm merely reported → damage shown in graphic bodily detail

members.gloss: harmed
members.tone: The flat report that harm was done, holding back every picture of it that *mangled* insists on showing.

members.gloss: scarred by battle
members.tone: Here the marks stand as proof of what was come through, so the damage reads as standing earned rather than harm suffered.

members.gloss: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
members.tone: Names the bruise by its two colours, homely and concrete beside the graver *livid*.

members.gloss: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
members.tone: The same pooled discoloration in a leaden, grim register that makes the skin sound like something has gone badly wrong beneath it, where *black-and-blue* keeps it almost domestic.

members.gloss: separated at the joint
members.tone: Structural and bloodless: the joint has come apart, and the word says nothing at all about pain.

members.gloss: separated at the joint
members.tone: The exact term for a joint driven out of place, diagnostic where *disjointed* sounds merely come-apart.

members.gloss: separated at the joint
members.tone: The barest statement of the same parting at the joint — it neither winces nor diagnoses.

members.gloss: having been disembowelled
members.tone: The most graphic member: the body opened and emptied, damage gone past anything that could still be called a wound.

members.gloss: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
members.tone: The softest word here for real physical injury - it carries the gloss's lean toward battle lightly, and shows nothing of the wound itself.

members.gloss: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
members.tone: Graver and more formal than *hurt* for the same injury, dignifying the damage and letting the battlefield sit close without shutting out other harm.

members.gloss: having edges that are jagged from injury
members.tone: The clipped form for flesh left with jagged edges, cool in shape even though the picture it raises is not.

members.gloss: having edges that are jagged from injury
members.tone: The ordinary participle for that same ragged tearing, felt rather than measured, where *lacerate* stays curt.

members.gloss: having edges that are jagged from injury
members.tone: The most violent of these: the jagged edges read as wreckage, the thing ruined rather than merely cut.

members.gloss: having edges that are jagged from injury
members.tone: The plainest word for a ragged injured edge — it names the tearing and stops, where *mangled* piles on ruin.

members.gloss: having the surface exposed and painful
members.tone: Reports pain rather than shape: the covering is gone and what lies under it is left exposed and stinging, unlike the jagged-edge words beside it.

families.axis: suddenness that is jarring, violent or severe → plain quickness of onset

members.gloss: happening without warning or in a short space of time
members.tone: The plain member of the family, covering both arrival without warning and arrival in very little time, and passing no verdict on either.

members.gloss: exceedingly sudden and unexpected
members.tone: Pushes *sudden* past what anyone was braced for, so the speed itself becomes the complaint.

members.gloss: marked by abrupt transitions
members.tone: Faults the transitions as uneven rather than violent — the thing never settles, but nothing in it snaps.

members.gloss: marked by abrupt transitions
members.tone: Harsher than *choppy* on the same broken transitions: the movement snatches, and the word makes it sound ungoverned.

members.gloss: occurring unexpectedly and requiring urgent action
members.tone: Flat and functional beside *explosive* — the unexpectedness registers only because it compels urgent action, not because it startles.

members.gloss: sudden and loud
members.tone: Puts noise into the suddenness, so where *abrupt* merely catches you unready this one goes off.

members.gloss: sudden and severe
members.tone: Grave rather than merely fast: severity is bolted to the speed, so the word reads as a warning.

members.gloss: very sudden and in great amount or degree
members.tone: Measures how far the change went as well as how fast it came, which is the dimension *sudden* leaves out.

families.axis: wrongness merely stated → cruelty fit for hell

members.gloss: morally bad or wrong
members.tone: The bare verdict: it names the wrongness itself and says nothing of the manner, which is what *atrocious* and *fiendish* are for.

members.gloss: shockingly brutal or cruel
members.tone: The shock sits inside the word, so the brutality is reported as something that appals rather than as something merely wrong.

members.gloss: shockingly brutal or cruel
members.tone: Formal and bookish where *atrocious* is loud, delivering the same charge of brutality in a cold register.

members.gloss: shockingly brutal or cruel
members.tone: The weightiest of these - the brutality is felt as damage done rather than as spectacle, where *atrocious* reaches for the outrage.

members.gloss: shockingly brutal or cruel
members.tone: Puts the cruelty outside the human, judging the doer as a kind of creature rather than as someone behaving badly.

members.gloss: characterized by wickedness or immorality
members.tone: The plainest word in the set made to carry wickedness, and the flatness is its force — *monstrous* shouts where this one only states.

members.gloss: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
members.tone: Absolute and unshaded: the wickedness is treated as total rather than as a streak, and no mitigation is offered.

members.gloss: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
members.tone: Suggestive rather than accusing, placing the evil behind what is visible — in what a thing comes out of as much as in the thing itself.

members.gloss: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
members.tone: Adds menace to the wickedness, so that what it names feels still in motion and threatening rather than simply condemned.

members.gloss: tending to corrupt or pervert
members.tone: Clinical in shape: it names an ongoing capacity to spoil rather than passing sentence on a single act.

members.gloss: tending to corrupt or pervert
members.tone: Harsher than *corruptive*, since what it names does not merely degrade a thing but bends it out of true.

members.gloss: tending to corrupt or pervert
members.tone: Makes the influence contagious — something to be kept clear of, not just something to disapprove of.

members.gloss: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
members.tone: Attributes the cruelty to a nature rather than a choice, as though it were the whole of what the thing is.

members.gloss: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
members.tone: Puts design behind the cruelty: intelligence at work, not the blind brutality of *atrocious*.

members.gloss: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
members.tone: The longer form of *diabolic*, and the extra syllable gives it room to sound theatrical rather than clinical.

members.gloss: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
members.tone: The most gleeful of these: the cruelty is relished, ingenuity taking pleasure in itself.

families.axis: neutral statement of non-equality → imbalance felt as a fault or unfairness

members.gloss: poorly balanced or matched in quantity or value or measure
members.tone: Carries a fault inside the measurement - poorly balanced or matched, not merely different - where *nonequivalent* only records that the quantities fail to agree.

members.gloss: having unsymmetrical parts or unequal dimensions or measurements
members.tone: Technical and cool: it states that parts are out of symmetry or dimensions come out unequal, and stops there without calling either a defect.

members.gloss: having unsymmetrical parts or unequal dimensions or measurements
members.tone: The plain-spoken counterpart to *anisometric* for the same condition of parts or measurements, describing the lack of match rather than complaining of it.

members.gloss: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
members.tone: Of a contest or the contestants in it, this puts the fault in the pairing itself - these two should never have been set against each other.

members.gloss: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
members.tone: Softer than *mismatched* for the same unfair contest: it notes that the thing tilts one way without condemning the making of the match.

members.gloss: not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity, or significance
members.tone: A flat denial rather than a complaint - the two are not equal and not interchangeable in value, quantity or significance, and the gap between them goes unjudged.

members.gloss: having a better than even chance of success
members.tone: The one member where the imbalance is good news: the chance of success runs better than even, so the tilt reads as advantage rather than defect.

members.gloss: debits and credits are not equal
members.tone: Strictly the ledger sense - debits failing to answer credits - which lands as an error in the books rather than as a neutral difference.

members.gloss: not caused to be equal
members.tone: Points at what was not done rather than at the result: no levelling has been applied, where *unequal* passes judgement on the gap that remains.

members.gloss: not caused to be equal
members.tone: The British spelling of *unequalized* and just as unjudging - it says only that nothing was made equal.

families.axis: merely past its freshness → rotted, foul and crawling

members.gloss: lacking freshness, palatability, or showing deterioration from age
members.tone: The plainest word here for the whole slide out of freshness — taste gone, condition gone with age — without yet ruling the food inedible the way *bad* does.

members.gloss: (of eggs) no longer edible
members.tone: A flat verdict on an egg: not merely aging but past eating, and far blunter about it than *stale*.

members.gloss: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
members.tone: The blankest possible condemnation — no mold, no smell, no rot named, just the ruling that the food can no longer be eaten or used.

members.gloss: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
members.tone: Frames the same loss — no longer edible or usable — as damage done to the food, a ruin rather than *bad*'s bare verdict.

members.gloss: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
members.tone: British spelling of *spoiled*, identical in force and equally final about food past eating or using.

members.gloss: having lost freshness through passage of time
members.tone: Understated to the edge of euphemism - it says only that time has passed and the freshness with it, leaving the conclusion *stale* states outright unsaid.

members.gloss: not fresh today
members.tone: Purely a matter of the calendar — it dates the food and leaves the verdict unspoken, where *stale* delivers one.

members.gloss: dried out
members.tone: Registers loss of moisture rather than any foulness, so the fault it names is one of texture and carries none of the disgust in *rotten* or *rancid*.

members.gloss: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
members.tone: Disgust made literal: the ruin is not merely named but shown, with the flies' eggs and larvae sitting on it.

members.gloss: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
members.tone: Carries the same infestation as *flyblown*, eggs and larvae alike, but puts the crawling larvae in front of you, which makes it the harder of the two to hear.

members.gloss: covered with or smelling of mold
members.tone: A specific and repellent charge — the growth seen on the food or smelled off it — where *bad* offers only a ruling.

members.gloss: covered with or smelling of mold
members.tone: British spelling of *moldy*, just as exact about mold either seen or smelled.

members.gloss: covered with or smelling of mold
members.tone: The gentlest of the three words for this condition, charging the same mold on the food or smell of mold off it with none of *moldy*'s bluntness.

members.gloss: (used of decomposing oils or fats) having a rank smell or taste usually due to a chemical change or decomposition
members.tone: Fixes on fats and oils gone over and on the rank smell or taste that gives them away, a sensory accusation rather than *bad*'s bare ruling.

members.gloss: having decayed or disintegrated; usually implies foulness
members.tone: The word for full collapse — decay carried through to disintegration, and foulness with it.

members.gloss: touched by rot or decay
members.tone: Formal, almost delicate for what it names: rot or decay has only touched the thing, not finished it as in *rotten*.
